notes: §1985:XIII.3.19.4 GR4: 'The report writer control system moves the data contained in the sum counter, according to the rules of the MOVE statement, to the printable item for presentation.' ReportWriterEmitter.TransferImage's FieldSumSource arm converts the counter (sized by ReportSectionBinder.SumCounterDigits) to the printable item through move.ConvertSource, a MOVE when no ROUNDED phrase is written, and CobolReport.SumPresentable answers true below 2002 (DialectBehavior.SumSizeErrorBlanksPrintableItem, kb/Work PB5248), so a 1985 size error never blanks the item. Probes (work-rr-04/s4a.cob, one CONTROL FOOTING FINAL over two GENERATEs): d) ZZ9.99 ' 42.00'; unsigned 999 of a -25 sum '025'; -ZZ9 and +ZZ9 '- 25'; alphanumeric X(5) '00042' and X(3) '042' (integer counter, GR1c); alphanumeric edited XXBXX '00 42'; 9V9 summing 1.25 and 2.37 '35' (truncating additions); f) 18 digits 999999999999999998 + 1 prints 999999999999999999; a named counter altered by ADD 100 in the procedure division prints 142 (GR6); a 99 counter overflowing (60 + 50) keeps 60 at 85, which §1985 leaves undefined (no ON SIZE ERROR), and is spaces at --std 2023. c) the 2023 ROUNDED phrase compiles at 85 (s4b) and turns the MOVE into a rounded COMPUTE: the 9V9 entry prints 37 where the 1985 MOVE prints 35; SUM OF (s4c) and an expression addend 'SUM W-DEC + 1' (s4d, prints 55) also compile, all PB5242's. Classes a, b, e have no arm in a sum-to-item move. The witness prints ZZ9.99 sums 12.00/30.00/42.00. kb/Work PB5242 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-reread2/rr-04.json).

next.reason: 1985: "The report writer control system moves the data contained in the sum counter, according to the rules of the MOVE statement"; 2023: "If the associated size error indicator is set, an EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE exception condition is set to exist and the printable item is filled with spaces.". Both treat the sum counter as a source item moved by MOVE rules. 2023 adds a ROUNDED case computed by COMPUTE rules, and on size error it fills the item with spaces instead of moving.
